posts.author: tiresias
posts.content_md:
I have two small commercially available holograms hanging on my kitchen wall. They've been there about 15 years and have been fine all that time.

Then a few weeks ago I noticed that one of them had heavy vertical streaking which looked as if it had started from the bottom. It looks like thin vertical strips some reaching almost to the top of the image. The bottom of the image is amost completely obscured by this streaking.

The other hologram is hangimg immediately below it, and it is fine.

I've asked if anyone's been near it with cleaning materials or spray, but non-one has. It seems odd that it has been OK for all these years and then suddenly degraded so badly within a few weeks.

Has anyone encountered this before, or know what is likely to have caused it?

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md: I have been helping clean up and organize TJ's hologram collection and lab, and the amount of hologram decay is depressing. Some things have obviously been lit with bright lights and have reticulated, and even on stuff that has been kept in drawers and not lit are developing odd streaks, maybe like the ones noted above. I've also seen random spots appear on unmounted holos that have been stored in the original Agfa packaging they came in, so it's a real bummer to see things go south without any reason! How to fix it, I don't know, we washed some stuff and re-Photo Flo-ed them, but still stuff gets in the image.

posts.author: tiresias
posts.content_md:
Here are a couple of photos of the streaky hologram.

It shows a computer keyboard with a mouse sitting above it - as you move the viewing angle the mouse changes into a mouse! I believe it's a quite common commercial hologram. It is mounted on a hardboard backing with a cardboard mount (visible around the photos) and a glass front.

hologram1.jpg was taken from slightly above the horizontal axis, and hologram2.jpg from just below it.

This has all just happened within the last few weeks. It has always hung in the same place with the same lighting for the last 15 years with no previous sign of degradation. And another hologram I bought at the same time is hanging just below it and that is still OK.

Any thoughts?

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: Looks like machine processing marks to me. The only holograms I have in my collection that show any flaws are the two "Stations of the Cross" plates from Advanced Holographics and a few polaroid holograms. The holograms on polaroid material have some really ugly processing marks like that. The Stations holograms are on silver halide material, and look like the vinyl backing's adhesive is damaging the emulsion. Yours id the worst I've seen though.

posts.author: tiresias
posts.content_md:
It's a complete mystery. I've taken the frame apart and the hologram film is stuck to the back of the cardboard mount with what looks like 4 strips of heavy duty transparent sticky-tape along the 4 sides. The film itself seems to have a black opaque back - I don't know if it is an itegral part of the film or some sort of backing. The sticky tape is stuck for half its width to the black back of the film and the other half of its width to the cardboard mount.

The film back looks clean and dry without marks or stains. The stick-tape looks clean too. No signs of anything leaking in or out.

Utterly bizzare!!!

I guess the glue from the sticky-tape could have somehow leached into the film from its edges, but it seems strange that it took years for the process to start and then took just a few weeks to spread across the whole surface.

Incidentally it may be closer to 10 (not 15) years that they've been hanging on the wall - not that it makes much difference to the mystery.

It's obviously not caused by machine processing, unless the damage is somehow following previously invisible markings in the film.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I know the problem. Your wife or cleaning lady took the glass off the front to clean both sides of the glass and saw the hologram needed cleaning and tried to wipe it with a wet cleaning agent. She saw the streaks and immediately put the glass back on the front and erased any signs of tampering. That's also why the second hologram is not damaged. She decided it best not to perform the cleaning on the second one. I would dust for fingerprints and hire a good CSI agent.

.

.

.

.

.

.

.

but seriously, it does look like machine or squeegy marks. It could have been that the streaks are actually slightly damaged areas that are not fully visible when the hologram is completely dry. It may be that the black paint on the back has finally failed every so slightly as to allow moisture to get in. I wonder if you put the hologram into a desiccator to pull out all moisture if the streaks will go away. If they do, then you can repaint or seal the back and edges again after drying the hologram fully out. A desiccator should not harm a hologram. Other techniques of drying may cause irreversable damage. But please do not hold me responsible if the desiccator damages the hologram for some unknown reason. Perform remedial steps only if you cannot live with the hologram as is. At least if you monitor the hologram in the desiccator and it seems to get better you know it's a moisture thingy. Did you environment change in the last two weeks toward a higher humidity? Good luck and peace!

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Interesting! How could bright green streaks form in previously dark areas unless new fringes had appeared? Do you know if this is a silver halide or photopolymer hologram? How does it look under normal daylight illumination (not as a hologram) - any sign of film damage? The streaks definitely look mechanical, but whether it was from the original film coating process or later lamination is unknown.

Could it have been made by this studio? [http://www.holostudios.com/studiofile/intstock.htm](http://www.holostudios.com/studiofile/intstock.htm) (R16 is the mouse) If so, contact them - they may have some ideas about what's going on. You shouldn't demand or expect a free replacement for a mass-consumer kitsch artifact after 15 years, but they may be able to help other holographers to avoid this problem in future if they have isolated the cause. If they have any insight on this, please post.
